text: A variable is a name that refers to a value. Create one with assignment, e.g. age = 21. The name goes on the left of = and the value on the right.
Core Python types: int (whole numbers), float (decimals), str (text), bool (True/False), list, tuple, dict and set. type(x) tells you the type.
/ always gives a float, // is floor division, % is the remainder and ** is power. == compares two values and returns True or False.
A for loop repeats once per item in a sequence; range(start, stop, step) stops before stop. A while loop repeats while its condition is True. break leaves the loop; continue skips to the next round.
if, elif and else are checked from top to bottom and only the first True branch runs. Indentation marks each block.
A function is defined with def name(parameters): and returns a value with return. Without return it gives back None. Default parameters are used when an argument is left out.
Lists are ordered and changeable. Indexing starts at 0 and negative indexes count from the end. Slices a[1:3] stop before the end index.
A dictionary maps unique keys to values. d[key] raises KeyError when the key is missing; d.get(key, default) returns the default instead.
A set stores unique items only and tests membership very quickly.
try runs code that might fail, except handles a named error, and finally always runs afterwards for clean-up. ValueError means the right type but an unusable value.
A class is a blueprint and an object is an instance of it. __init__ runs when an object is created. self is the object the method was called on. Inheritance lets a child class reuse a parent class.
A list comprehension builds a list in one line: [expression for item in sequence if condition].
Big-O describes how work grows with input size n: O(1) constant, O(log n) halving, O(n) one loop, O(n log n) efficient sorting, O(n²) nested loops.
Linear search checks every item, O(n). Binary search halves a sorted list each step, O(log n).
Bubble sort swaps neighbours repeatedly, O(n²). Merge sort splits, sorts halves and merges them, O(n log n).
A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem and needs a base case that stops the calls.
Lists keep order; sets and dicts give fast lookups; a stack is last-in-first-out; a queue is first-in-first-out.
Supervised learning uses labelled examples; unsupervised learning finds structure without labels; reinforcement learning learns from rewards.
Models are fitted on training data and checked on unseen test data. Overfitting means memorising the training data; underfitting means the model is too simple.
Generative AI creates new content. LLMs predict the next word and can hallucinate — produce fluent but false statements — so important outputs need human review.

Responsible AI covers fairness, transparency, privacy, accountability and safety. Bias usually comes from unrepresentative data, and proxy features can carry bias even when a protected attribute is removed.
GDPR governs personal data. The EU AI Act is risk-based: banned uses, high-risk uses with strict duties, and lighter transparency duties for lower-risk uses.
Start from a business problem with measurable value, check data readiness, pilot small, involve stakeholders, then scale with governance.
Kotter's 8 steps: create urgency, form a guiding coalition, create a vision, communicate it, remove obstacles, create short-term wins, build on the change, anchor it in culture.
SWOT: internal strengths and weaknesses, external opportunities and threats. PESTLE: political, economic, social, technological, legal, environmental.
Porter's Five Forces: rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, buyer power and supplier power. Barriers to entry protect incumbents.
The 4Ps are product, price, place and promotion. STP means segmentation, targeting and positioning.
Profit = revenue − costs. Gross margin = (revenue − COGS) ÷ revenue. ROI = (gain − cost) ÷ cost. Cash flow tracks real money in and out.
A KPI is a measurable indicator tied to a strategic goal, with a clear owner.
Transformational leaders inspire with vision; transactional leaders use rewards; servant leaders put the team first; situational leaders adapt to the team.
When stuck: restate the question in your own words, underline key terms, eliminate options you know are wrong, and test what is left against a small example.
